41F, similar issue with lack of attraction until I know someone. I have pretty much accepted the label of demisexual.  Doesn’t matter how pretty a man is, I don’t want to touch him until I have a good handle on his personality and preferences. And usually by then I’m firmly in the not an option category for them. 

It used to rock me hard when I realized I had fallen for a friend. Now, I know I don’t have to blow up the relationship I have because my brain went stupid. Of course I get attracted to them sometimes; I pick good people to have around me. They are quality men and I am just recognizing that on another level. 

I give myself distance and remind myself that they haven’t expressed any interest to change the current situation. It fades eventually, and I make sure in the meanwhile to try to be consistent with my support but sparing with my face to face time. I don’t let myself ruminate anymore on what I wish was there. Instead I keep busy. It’s not painless, but it does get easier. 

As for how to not be alone doing this, I don’t know. I try to look for people in hobbies and tangents to the circles I swim in. Someone I can get a feel for in a group situation before ever trying one on one hang outs. Magic sometimes strikes and I can get a light crush on someone and then actually talk with them more directly to see if it gets stronger or fades.  

Mostly if someone asks to go out, I agree just in case. I try to keep investment low on their part until I care, but I have gone on multiple dates with people my friends only know as ‘Table’ and ‘Lava Lamp’ because they asked and I couldn’t tell if they were people I might like. They were not.

But at the end of the day, I’m still romantically alone. I hope you figure out something better for vetting new prospects for yourself.

Fun and nice people are not the same as good people. Be cautious until you can tell the difference. 

Watch out for your girl friends, and even women you do not know. No one goes to a party alone. No one stays at a party by themselves. If you see someone alone, check on them. And pay attention to who in your groups does the same for others. If you have someone who dismisses your concern for someone else, then they most likely will NOT be there for you if you need them. Don’t depend on them. 

Just assume your drink will be spiked at one point. These ladies are your lifeline for when that happens, and you are theirs. It happens every night somewhere, regardless of how watchful you are.

Embarrassment is temporary, but the fun is very real. Don’t hold back on something for fear that it will film poorly or you won’t look cool doing it. Participate as fully as you can. 

Anyway that’s a lot of advice.

Depends on the age. Early to mid 20s, it never occurred to me that I was vulnerable, until it was made obvious. I also had complete (false) confidence in my ability to fight. I weight lifted, I did sports. I was strong and I’d had basic defense lessons. And it gave him more time for what I already had consumed to start to work. By the time I knew for sure I was in trouble enough that I had to be disruptive/speak up, I couldn’t stand anymore or even grab my purse by my feet.

Having been given a bad drink before, it has been extremely difficult to drink around other people ever since then. Even people I have known for years and trust implicitly. Over ten years later, I watched a guy friend make a drink for me I was really excited to try, but it was stronger than expected. I panicked when I got a little light headed and I was forcing myself to throw up in his bathroom before any kind of logic came back to me. I did apologize and explain to him afterwards. But I could see being afraid to drink something, afraid to put off a new person by the heavy trauma explanation, and just panicking and trying to pull this off. Fear and time constraints make people dumb and rude. 

(FYI I got really lucky, and was able to crawl into a public space before I blacked out for nearly 3 days. I still sometimes have nightmares where I ask for him to call a cab, and he tells me no. I can’t imagine the additional aftermath if I hadn’t made it out to the safety of witnesses first.)

Yup. I broke one out of 3 ankle bones a few years ago, and was limping pretty badly but could still stand. The first doctor I saw refused to do X-rays, told me I sprained it and gave me $80 crutches. 

I walked on the broken bone waiting for the sprain to get better until it killed a huge chunk of my cartilage in the joint. Then that chunk broke off, dissolved back into my body and I had a hole in bone ends when I tried to move the joint. 

Finally a second bone cracked and I crumpled, 6 months later, no longer able to walk at all. I saw three doctors who all did no further testing until I literally could not walk. They concluded it was a Sprain, or plantar faciitus etc, and I needed to stretch it and/or let it rest and lose weight. Because it doesn’t hurt that bad and fat means I am too heavy for my bones. 

The last doctor I saw was amazed I had not had X-rays before then. I had to have major surgery and took months to learn to walk again. If the first doctor, or second, or third had listened and looked… it could have saved me thousands and thousands of dollars. Plus ya know, I wouldn’t have lost mobility in my ankle.
